items.say: Hi, I'm Clover. Copy me, nice and easy.
text: A few gentle moves to wake your body up: neck, shoulders, arms and sides.
Each move has a little timer. Go at your own pace, and make the moves as small as feels good.
Rests come in between. Stand, or sit on a sturdy chair: both work.

items.say: Strength time. Your own body is all the kit we need.
text: Wall push-ups, squats and marching on the spot. Slow and steady is better than lots.
The count is a guide, not a target. Stop early whenever you like, and rest as long as you want.
A sturdy chair behind you makes squats easier: just touch it and stand back up.

items.say: Stretching. The slowest thing we do. I'm a big fan.
text: Ease into each stretch until you feel a gentle pull, then hold it and breathe.
No bouncing, and no forcing. A stretch should feel good, never sharp.
If one side feels different from the other, that's normal.

items.say: Desk o'clock! Let's loosen the bits that sit still all day.
text: Slow, small moves for your neck, shoulders and upper back. Handy after a long sit.
Sit tall on a sturdy chair, or stand: both work. Turn and tilt only as far as feels easy.
Side to side is plenty. We never roll the head all the way round.

items.say: Chair day! Every move happens on a chair. Best furniture there is.
text: Every move here is done sitting on a sturdy chair. One without wheels, please.
Sit near the front of the seat with your feet flat on the floor, and hold the sides when you like.
Standing up comes last, and only if it feels fine. Use your hands on the chair to help.

items.say: Balance time. I'm a rabbit, so I'm mostly balance. And ears.
text: Stand beside a wall or a sturdy chair back, and keep a hand on it or near it the whole time.
Hold on as much as you like. Holding on is how these are done.
A wobble is normal. If you feel unsteady, put your foot down and hold on.

neck-tilt.name: Neck tilts
how: Ear towards your shoulder, slowly.
Pause for a breath, then over to the other side.
Shoulders stay low. Small is fine.

shoulder-roll.name: Shoulder rolls
how: Lift your shoulders up towards your ears.
Roll them back, then let them drop.
Arms hang loose.

reach-up.name: Reach up
how: Arms up high, like you're picking fruit from a tall tree.
Breathe out and lower.
Staying seated works too.

side-bend-left.name: Side bend, left
how: Right arm up and over.
Lean gently to the left.
Feel the stretch along your side.

side-bend-right.name: Side bend, right
how: Left arm up and over.
Lean gently to the right.
Feel the stretch along your side.

march.name: March on the spot
how: Lift your knees at an easy pace.
Let your arms swing.
Low knees are fine.

wall-push.name: Wall push-ups
how: Hands on the wall at shoulder height.
Bend your elbows and lean in.
Push back to the start.

squat.name: Squats
how: Feet hip-width.
Sit back like there's a chair behind you.
Stand tall.

lunge-left.name: Lunge stretch, left leg
how: Step your left foot forward.
Bend that knee a little.
Feel the stretch in the back leg's hip.

lunge-right.name: Lunge stretch, right leg
how: Step your right foot forward.
Bend that knee a little.
Easy does it.

neck-turn.name: Neck turns
how: Sit tall, shoulders down.
Slowly turn your head to look towards one shoulder.
Back to the middle, then the other way. Only as far as is easy.

chest-stretch.name: Chest stretch
how: Sit tall, arms out to the sides.
Draw your shoulders back and down.
Lift your chest a little and breathe.

twist.name: Upper-body twist
how: Cross your arms, hands on your shoulders.
Slowly turn your upper body to one side. Hips stay still.
Back to the middle, then the other side.

seated-march.name: Seated march
how: Sit tall and hold the sides of the chair.
Lift one knee a little, then lower it gently.
Now the other. Small lifts are fine.

ankle-stretch.name: Ankle stretch
how: Hold the sides of the chair.
Straighten one leg, foot off the floor. Point your toes away, then towards you.
Lower it, then the other leg.

sit-to-stand.name: Sit to stand
how: Sit near the front of the chair, feet flat.
Lean forward a little and slowly stand up. Hands on the chair if you like.
Sit back down, nice and slow.

heel-raise.name: Heel raises
how: One hand on the wall or a chair back.
Slowly rise up onto your toes.
Lower your heels, nice and slow.

side-leg-lift.name: Side leg lifts
how: One hand on the wall or a chair back. Stand tall.
Lift one leg a little out to the side, then lower it.
Now the other leg.

one-leg-stand.name: One-leg stand
how: Fingertips on the wall or a chair back.
Lift one foot just off the floor and hold.
Put it down whenever you like, then the other foot.
